Row.Text: In the eye of each Ottoman leader, each warlord and mayor, each shopkeeper and merchant, shines the dream that they, perhaps, might one day rise to power. These conditions are useful for individual drive – less so for the formation of a centralized state.
The road to unity will be difficult. Each ghazi and each bey must be courted, bribed, cajoled, persuaded or perhaps threatened. Nonetheless, it will be done.
It is precisely in this drive that the Ottomans will rise.

Horns sound through the wood, as foresters scatter. The Ottoman hunt begins, as hoca and bey lead their horses at breakneck speed, chasing boar, jackal or tiger - but willing to send arrows after any woodsman in their path.
Control these lesser nobles. This is not conducive to peace.
Encourage the hunt. It fosters bravery through all of the Ottoman hierarchy.
